rows: Secured on Railway Properties and Income
Chinese Imp. Railways 5 p.c. Gold Loan of 1899 (Peiping-Mukden)
Redeemable in equal annual instalments of £57,500 ending August 1, 1944. Secured on properties and earnings of Peiping-Mukden railways.
Chinese Imp. Government 5 p.c. Gold Loan of 1902 (Shansi Railway)
Issued in December, 1903, in Paris. Redeemable by 20 annual instalments, ending March 1, 1932. Secured on the railway properties and earnings. (Line from Chengting-fu to Taiyuanfu.)
Imp. Chinese Railways, Shanghai-Nanking Line, 5 p.c. of 1904 and 1907.

Repayable by 25 annual equal instalments of £116,000 each, from December, 1929, to December, 1953. Secured on the properties and earnings of railway. Issued in 1904 £2,250,000, subscribers receiving one net-profit sub-certificate to bearer for every bond allotted, conferring the right to participate in the net profits of the railway. A second issue of £650,000 was made in 1907.
Chinese Imp. Government Honan Railway 5 p.c. Gold Loan of 1905.
Redeemable between 1916 and 1935 by 20 annual drawings. Secured by a first charge on railway properties and earnings. Line from Taokow to Chinghua, operated by Pekin Syndicate.
Chinese Imp. Government 5 p.c. Gold Loans of 1903 and 1907. (Pienlo Railway)

Redeemable by drawings commencing in 1915 and terminating in 1920, seven instalments of Frs. 2,500,000 each having been paid. Redemption started actually in 1935. Secured on railway's properties and earnings. Line from Kaifengfu to Honanfu.
Imp. Chinese Railways 5 p.c. Canton-Kowloon Railway Loan of 1907.
Redeemable by annual drawings commencing 1920 and ending 1937. First charge on railway's properties and earnings.
Imp. Chinese Government 5 p.c. Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway Loan of 1908.
Redeemable by annual drawings of £75,000 each, commencing 1918 and ending 1938. Secured on the revenues of the Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railway and the surplus earnings of the Peiping-Mukden Line.
